Google Material Design 3 (Material) implemented for Astro: 3-tier design tokens, local Roboto typography, 5 scaffold slots, and edge-native CMS parity.

# Material Design 3: Built for Modern Astro The official Material theme in Interstellar CMS implements Google’s Material Design 3 specification without compromise. ![Earth and space station satellite view from Unsplash](/images/uploads/2026/10/space-station.jpg) ## 3-Tier Design Tokens Design systems break when component implementations leak into brand tokens. Interstellar enforces a mathematical 3-tier token hierarchy: 1. **Reference Tokens (`md.ref.*`):** 13 tonal steps calculated using Google’s HCT (Hue, Chroma, Tone) perceptual algorithm. 2. **System Tokens (`md.sys.*`):** Semantic application roles: Primary, Secondary, Surface Containers (Lowest to Highest), and Elevation Levels 0 to 5. 3. **Component Tokens (`md.comp.*`):** Over 508 isolated properties mapping System tokens directly to individual components.
## 100% Shared Theme Parity Traditional CMS architectures suffer from visual drift: what editors see in the admin preview rarely matches the live website. In Interstellar CMS, both the public Astro site and the `/editor/` import the exact same tokens, fonts, and blocks from `@theme`. Keystrokes in the editor render with pixel-perfect accuracy against responsive device viewports.

Material Design 3: Built for Modern Astro

The official Material theme in Interstellar CMS implements Google’s Material Design 3 specification without compromise.

3-Tier Design Tokens

Design systems break when component implementations leak into brand tokens. Interstellar enforces a mathematical 3-tier token hierarchy:

  1. Reference Tokens (md.ref.*): 13 tonal steps calculated using Google’s HCT (Hue, Chroma, Tone) perceptual algorithm.
  2. System Tokens (md.sys.*): Semantic application roles: Primary, Secondary, Surface Containers (Lowest to Highest), and Elevation Levels 0 to 5.
  3. Component Tokens (md.comp.*): Over 508 isolated properties mapping System tokens directly to individual components.

100% Shared Theme Parity

Traditional CMS architectures suffer from visual drift: what editors see in the admin preview rarely matches the live website.

In Interstellar CMS, both the public Astro site and the /editor/ import the exact same tokens, fonts, and blocks from @theme. Keystrokes in the editor render with pixel-perfect accuracy against responsive device viewports.
